mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a single month is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during such spikes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10), or the S&P 500 closes higher than its pre-tightening 20-day average during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims exceeding 10,000 for three consecutive months coincides with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting investor concern about labor market weakening.
failure_condition: During such labor weakness regimes, the 60-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of instances, or the unemployment rate recovers faster than the S&P 500 (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be positive as investors anticipate future inflation compensation.
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the Sharpe ratio of the signal is below 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% followed by a rebound of at least 1.5% in the next month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as it signals a bottoming-out in supply constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -2% in month t, INDPRO > +1.5% in month t+1
failure_condition: This pattern occurs but the 60-day forward return is negative in >50% of cases, or the IC of the pattern vs. baseline is < -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3.5%, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as lower policy rates boost equity discounting.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10) during 5 such episodes, or the policy rate does not revert upward within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% in a month triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as market anticipates overheating labor markets and potential policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.0% in a month
failure_condition: During such episodes, the 5-day forward return is not negative in >80% of cases, or the unemployment rate recovers faster than the S&P 500 (IC > 0.07).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales ( proxy via HOUST > previous month) with no decline in the following month predict a positive S&P 500 forward return over 20 days as it signals resilient consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month for 2 consecutive months, and HOUST in third month >= previous month
failure_condition: Across 10 such demand streaks, the 20-day forward return is not positive (p > 0.05), or the pattern's IC is < 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in consumer confidence (captured via a proxy such as a leading index or sentiment series; here using HOUST as a stand-in for confidence proxy) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to conflicting supply and demand signals.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND HOUST > previous month
failure_condition: The interaction pattern occurs but the 60-day forward return is not negative in >60% of cases, or the IC of the interaction relative to the individual proxies is > 0.05.
